next_question: On the same credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, change the acquisition MECHANISM from same-host link-following BFS to SITE-NATIVE DISCOVERY channels (robots.txt sitemap directives, sitemap.xml, on-site search/query URLs, RSS/Atom feeds, and JSON-LD/structured-data enumeration): over a frozen multi-host pool that is separately confirmed to contain DEEP (hop>=3) state items on at least two distinct hosts/engines, what fraction of those DEEP items can be reached in <= K preregistered GETs (e.g. K=3: one discovery GET plus the item-page GET) using a site-native discovery channel alone, versus only by traversing the hop>=3 shortest path? Preregistered falsifier, arithmetically checkable before freeze and satisfiable in BOTH directions: if the O(1)-reachable fraction of DEEP state items is >= a preregistered materiality threshold (e.g. 0.50) on >=2 engines, then shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition and persistent path caching is not the optimization target (effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion); if that fraction is below the threshold, then even with site-native discovery, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound and persistence of paths/procedures retains a measurable, depth-dependent amortization surface whose break-even can be computed from a real re-derivation cost. This is materially orthogonal to EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 because it measures a different acquisition mechanism rather than re-scoring a link-following level-order estimator whose DEEP/NEAR ratio is forced by construction (VN-V9/VF-03). If the Global Research Director instead prefers the maintenance/invalidation axis, the alternative live question is: how does the cost of keeping a persisted path/procedure VALID between episodes (re-validation GETs/bytes plus the stale-replay false-accept rate) scale with hop and elapsed time relative to re-derivation.
